extracted.intended_audience: JABSOM Library users: students, faculty, clinicians, and researchers who use PubMed
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for searching, reading, accessing, saving, and filtering PubMed records (including finding full text, identifying peer-reviewed journals, saving searches/citations, and using tools like My NCBI, Clipboard, and Single Citation Matcher).

rubrics_metrics.name: How to read a PubMed citation
rubrics_metrics.description: Key parts of a PubMed citation include the article title, authors, journal name, publication date, volume and issue, page numbers, and DOI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these elements to identify and verify an article; the page includes a diagram showing each part of the citation to help locate bibliographic details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bracketed citations indicate non-English articles
rubrics_metrics.description: Bracketed citations are an indication that the article is written in a language other than English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When you see brackets around the citation information in PubMed, expect the original article language is not English and follow the link or record metadata for language and translation options.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get the full text of an article via institutional access
rubrics_metrics.description: Access PubMed from the JABSOM Library website to see icons for UH holdings (the Find It button). If no icons appear, check that you are connected via the JABSOM Library proxy URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative: set your institutional affiliation in your My NCBI account (Outside Tool) so PubMed shows your institution's holdings. Use the Find It button/icons to route to full text or library resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to determine what journals are indexed in PubMed/MEDLINE
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the NLM Catalog: 'Journals referenced in the NCBI Databases' to search for journals referenced in NCBI databases, including PubMed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visit 'Journal Selection for MEDLINE' to learn the specific criteria used to select a journal for admittance to MEDLINE (i.e., to understand indexing standards and inclusion criteria).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difference between MEDLINE and PubMed/PMC
rubrics_metrics.description: MEDLINE, PubMed, and PMC (PubMed Central) are distinct resources with different scope and content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the NLM Fact Sheet 'MEDLINE, PubMed, and PMC: How are they different?' to understand coverage, indexing, and differences in content and access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving a search in PubMed
rubrics_metrics.description: You can save a search in PubMed using your My NCBI account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the My NCBI page for information on saving searches; PubMed Help also provides instructions for saving a search as RSS feeds and for creating a URL to bookmark your search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving searches and citations and creating email alerts
rubrics_metrics.description: My NCBI lets you save searches to re-run or have mailed as automatic alerts, save article citations as collections or bibliographies, and set PubMed preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register for a free NCBI account and use My NCBI to manage saved searches, collections, bibliographies, and automated email alerts. Links to My NCBI are provided on the page.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to find peer-reviewed articles in PubMed
rubrics_metrics.description: Most journals indexed in PubMed are peer-reviewed, but PubMed does not provide a direct 'peer-reviewed' limiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Limits to eliminate letters, editorials, etc., then use Clinical Queries (on the Home page under find) — most remaining items will be peer-reviewed. Alternatively, use 'Journals in the NCBI Database' to look up a specific journal and visit the journal site to confirm peer-review status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find help using PubMed
rubrics_metrics.description: Help links are available at the top of all PubMed screens for general assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For additional help specific to your institution or more in-depth guidance, consult a librarian or email the JABSOM Library (hslinfo@hawaii.edu).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding a complete citation for a single article (Single Citation Matcher)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Single Citation Matcher (link at bottom of Home page and under More Resources on Advanced Search) to retrieve a full citation by filling in known information about a specific reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter known fields (author, journal, year, volume, page, etc.) into the Single Citation Matcher to locate the complete citation record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporarily saving citations with the Clipboard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Clipboard is a temporary holding file for all citations collected during your online session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select desired citations and use the 'Send to' link to save to Clipboard. Click the Clipboard link on the right side of the Results page to retrieve citations. Note: Clipboard contents are lost after 8 hours of inactivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Saving your search strategy (History and download)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your My NCBI account to save searches, or use History (found on the Advanced Search screen) to hold search strategies and results from your current session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: History has a 'Download history' option to save searches in .csv file format for later reuse or archival; use My NCBI for persistent saved searches across sessions.
